102: And now we shall explain the din of accepting lashon hara. The acceptance of lashon hara, which the Torah exhorted us against, is not to believe in one's heart that the thing [said] is true. There is no need to expatiate upon [the difference between] the nature of the accepter and [that of] the man whom he accepts about. For there is almost no difference. But, the principle of the thing, in short, is this. Every Jew is commanded not to accept lashon hara against any other Jew — except about heretics, informers, and the like — those who have left the category of "your fellow."
